rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (kd 0.05 to 0.30): the oval result was identical to the baseline (progress 0.115, max_error 0.0607, one line-loss event), so kd has no effect on the oval failure. The oval therefore fails from a sensing or recovery problem, not a damping problem. On s-bend and slalom, kd 0.30 raised progress (0.04 to 0.157 and 0.035 to 0.110) but also raised steering_oscillation to 0.154 and 0.158, just above the 0.15 threshold the Evaluator set. Max_error on s-bend rose to 0.0665. Every run still ends off track with one line-loss event. Changes: (1) kd from 0.30 to 0.15, the Evaluator's requested fix for oscillation above 0.15. This keeps some damping while cutting jitter. (2) Sensor spread widened from +/-0.04 m to +/-0.05 m (x = -0.05, -0.025, 0, 0.025, 0.05), with weights unchanged at -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1. The robot loses the line on sharp bends because the array reaches the tape edge too early, and a wider array should keep at least one sensor on tape for longer. The 25 mm spacing keeps the 12 mm footprints overlapping the 25 mm tape. Kp, ki, base_speed, weights and line_loss stay unchanged. I am deliberately changing two groups, kd and sensor layout, because the oval result shows kd cannot fix the oval and only one race per iteration is available. Expected result: oscillation falls back to about 0.10 or below, the oval changes from its baseline value, line-loss events fall on at least one track, and max_error stays below 0.06 on some tracks. Hypotheses to check: (a) a wider array reduces line-loss events on the oval; (b) kd 0.15 keeps the s-bend and slalom progress gains while steering_oscillation drops below 0.15. Next steps: if the robot still leaves the line with line_loss_events at 1, test line_loss = search_left or search_right. If it completes but completion_time is above 2.5 s, raise base_speed in steps of about 0.2.
